stations.name: glass insulator wire
instructions: Glass insulation passes essentially no power in CEE 1.1.3. Its dark lamp and near-zero meter reading are expected. The hanging-insulator item can also create a loose native endpoint on a PG terminal.

stations.name: Duplex and 12 V bulb
instructions: Use the duplex spool on the two terminations to reconnect the cable. Some voltage is lost in its wires. Measure current on a breakout wire; equal supply and return currents cancel around the whole cable. The spool retains CEE's native creative-only availability in 1.1.3.
To replace a burned PG bulb, click once to remove it and again with a healthy bulb to install it. Use a 12 V bulb here; ordinary bulbs are rated for 120 V. Switch the feed OFF before repairs.

stations.name: Lineman decorations
instructions: Hold the lineman's stick in your main hand and a banner or wire damper in your offhand, then click the wire. Shift-click with an empty offhand to remove the attachment. Decorations do not change electrical power.

stations.name: Three-pole energy
instructions: The 240 V supply feeds two equal 120 V lamps in series. Relative to their shared middle line, the red lamp is +120 V and the blue lamp is -120 V. Both consume power; the native three-pole meter sums about 60 W. Energy rises slowly in kWh. Turn the feed OFF to stop both lamps, then ON to resume. This is a split DC example; the alternator stations demonstrate AC phases.
